label: Extended Marxian political economy to imperialism and mass democratic spontaneity
description: Rosa Luxemburg developed Marx's reproduction schemas in Capital Vol. II into a structural theory of imperialism, while defending revolutionary mass democracy against bureaucratic centralism.
dialecticalTension: Pits democratic mass spontaneity against both parliamentary reformism and Leninist vanguard substitutionism.
historicalContext: Formulated in Reform or Revolution (1900), The Accumulation of Capital (1913), and The Russian Revolution (1918).

label: Inspired Arendt's council-democracy model and critique of party bureaucracy
description: Hannah Arendt devoted a celebrated portrait to Rosa Luxemburg in Men in Dark Times and drew directly on Luxemburg's defense of spontaneous revolutionary councils and political freedom ('freedom for the one who thinks differently').
dialecticalTension: Channels anti-authoritarian revolutionary councils into Arendtian civic republicanism.
historicalContext: Engaged across The Origins of Totalitarianism (1951), On Revolution (1963), and Men in Dark Times (1968).

label: Shaped Frankfurt School libertarian socialism and anti-imperialist critique
description: As a young soldier-council participant in Berlin 1918, Marcuse drew lifelong inspiration from Luxemburg's humanistic, anti-authoritarian Marxism against Stalinist orthodoxy.
dialecticalTension: Preserves emancipatory spontaneity against bureaucratic domination.
historicalContext: German Revolution of 1918–1919 and Frankfurt School critical theory.

label: Expanded historical materialism with a theory of global primitive accumulation
description: Luxemburg argued that Marx's primitive accumulation is not merely a pre-capitalist stage, but a continuous violent appropriation of non-capitalist peripheries required to realize surplus value.
dialecticalTension: Globalizes historical materialism to account for colonialism and imperialism.
historicalContext: Articulated in The Accumulation of Capital (1913).
